title: Filippo Maria Visconti → Francesco Sforza, ducal cipher slips on parchment (the last months of the Visconti duke)
correspondents: Filippo Maria Visconti, Duke of Milan → Francesco Sforza
folio_note: about 14 parchment slips entirely in cipher, c. 10-15 lines each (f. 5 seen: c. 15 lines of letters and signs, no word division); siblings ff. 5/6 and 8/9 (ital. 1584) and 130/131 (ital. 1583) have the decipherment filed on the next leaf
status: Mazzatinti: 'In cifre: membran.' for each; 'Traduzione della lettera precedente' only after ff. 5, 8 (1584) and 130 (1583). Image check: f. 15 is followed by a clear f. 16 of the same date (probably its decipherment, unlisted). ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 are DECODE R7902, R7907 (Non-decrypted). The ital. 1583 slips (ff. 110, 136, 162; DECODE R7902, R7907) are catalogued separately with the other ital. 1583 Visconti letters (venice_milan_decode row 0); this entry is the ital. 1584 slips.
why: The Visconti chancery archive and its ciphers were destroyed in 1447; these slips, with three filed decipherments, are the route to Filippo Maria's own cipher and the 1447 negotiations that brought Sforza to Milan; anything read before 1449 would also be the oldest reading in the project.
score_note: Scored from Mazzatinti, Inventario dei mss. italiani II (1887) pp. 285-509, during the Oct 2026 venice_milan_print sweep (research/venice_milan_print/, sforza_list.txt)
verify: View each slip on Gallica (canvas = folio + 2 to 4 at the start) and note whether a decipherment follows; rebuild the key from ff. 5/6 and 8/9; read the slips without one.
prior_art: open as far as checked (28 Oct 2026: cryptiana unsolved.htm mentions only ital. 1584 f. 68/69 and key DECODE R1857; DECODE has only ital. 1583 ff. 68-158, R7898-R7915; known.py no hit for ital. 1584-1591). Many leaves carry interlinear or filed contemporary decipherments that Mazzatinti does not always note (seen: 1584 f. 15 followed by an unlisted clear f. 16 of the same date; a cipher block on canvas 235 has interlinear glosses), so 'read at the time' must be ruled out leaf by leaf.

title: Andrea da Birago → Francesco Sforza, a wholly ciphered letter from Pavia
correspondents: Andrea da Birago → Francesco Sforza
shelfmark: BnF italien 1585, f. 33 (Gallica canvas 63; address on 64)
folio_note: one letter, 12 lines of cipher after a clear salutation, signed 'Servitor Andreas Biragus'; a third alphabet (signs built from H, A, 6, 00 and dashes), unlike Amidani's, Guarna's or Tranchedini's; f. 32 is a clear letter of the same writer and day (probably a separate letter)
status: Image checked 29 Oct 2026: no late clear copy on ff. 31-34 and no interlinear glosses; Mazzatinti lists it under Amidani's 'del medesimo' chain.
why: Pavia under the Ambrosian Republic, Feb 1448; the one leaf of the 1447-48 Milan series found with no decipherment.
score_note: Scored from Mazzatinti, Inventario dei mss. italiani II (1887) pp. 285-509, during the Oct 2026 venice_milan_print sweep (research/venice_milan_print/, sforza_list.txt)
verify: Compare f. 32 (same writer, same day) as a possible crib; look for Birago's other letters and a Birago key (ASMi cart. 1597 keys on DECODE).
prior_art: open as far as checked (28 Oct 2026: cryptiana unsolved.htm mentions only ital. 1584 f. 68/69 and key DECODE R1857; DECODE has only ital. 1583 ff. 68-158, R7898-R7915; known.py no hit for ital. 1584-1591). Many leaves carry interlinear or filed contemporary decipherments that Mazzatinti does not always note (seen: 1584 f. 15 followed by an unlisted clear f. 16 of the same date; a cipher block on canvas 235 has interlinear glosses), so 'read at the time' must be ruled out leaf by leaf. Leaf-by-leaf check 29 Oct 2026: no copy or gloss beside it (research/venice_milan_print/ital1584_copies_B.md).
